svg.title: One local KSG term is an exact rational
svg.desc: The local KSG term for n = 16 and k = 3 as a difference of harmonic numbers: Euler's constant cancels, the term lies in a sharp box, and only two endpoint cells are zero.

g.font-family: 'Source Sans Pro', 'Source Sans 3', 'Latin Modern Math', 'Helvetica Neue', Arial, sans-serif
g.text: ONE LOCAL KSG TERM IS AN EXACT RATIONAL
(a) The local term T for n = 16, k = 3
x = nX + 1
y = nY + 1
+D
−D
zero
Dashed frontier: x + y = n + k.
Beyond it: unreachable if the conditional lemma holds.
(b) Why it is exact
For positive integers, ψ(m) = Hm−1 − γ (DLMF 5.4.14), with
harmonic numbers Hj = 1 + 1/2 + … + 1/j. Euler's γ cancels:
T = ψ(k) + ψ(n) − ψ(x) − ψ(y)
Sharp box: −D ≤ T ≤ D, D = Hn−1 − Hk−1 = 1.818 here.
Zeros: only the two endpoint cells (k, n) and (n, k).
On the 8,198-row pid-rs corpus, all 354 zeros satisfy this
endpoint rule, certified modulo three primes; a fourth prime
was rejected because it made nonzero terms vanish.
Dashed line: a conditional lemma, not yet promoted, says
counts beyond x + y = n + k are unreachable.
Color: teal positive, wine negative, strength |T|/D. The identity bounds one arithmetic term; it proves nothing about neighbor search, bias or PID atoms.
